questiontext.text: Addition of water to alkynes occurs in acidic medium and in the presence of \(\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}\) ions as a catalyst. Which of the following products will be formed on addition of water to but-1-yne under these conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydration of terminal alkynes in the presence of dilute sulfuric acid and mercuric sulfate catalyst follows Markovnikov's rule. Electrophilic addition of a proton to the terminal carbon forms the more stable secondary carbocation intermediate, followed by nucleophilic attack of water at the internal carbon.

Step 2: Evaluation
For but-1-yne, \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}\), addition of water across the triple bond yields an enol intermediate, but-1-en-2-ol:
\[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}^+} \left[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CH}_2\right]\]The enol spontaneously tautomerizes to the thermodynamically more stable ketone, butan-2-one (ethyl methyl ketone):
\[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CH}_2 \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The product formed on hydration of but-1-yne under these acidic conditions is butan-2-one, \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{CH}_3\).

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds is most reactive towards nucleophilic addition reactions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition reactions is determined by two factors: electronic effects (magnitude of the electrophilic partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon) and steric effects (spatial crowding around the carbonyl group during tetrahedral transition state formation).

Step 2: Evaluation
Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because ketones have two electron-donating alkyl or aryl groups that reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon by inductive or resonance effects, while also causing greater steric hindrance. Furthermore, aliphatic aldehydes are more reactive than aromatic aldehydes because resonance interaction between the aromatic ring and the carbonyl group disperses the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, diminishing its electrophilicity. Therefore, ethanal has a significantly more electrophilic and less sterically crowded carbonyl carbon than acetone, benzaldehyde, or acetophenone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ethanal, \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{H}\), is the most reactive compound towards nucleophilic addition reactions.

questiontext.text: The correct order of increasing acidic strength is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acidic strength depends directly on the stability of the conjugate base formed after proton donation. A more stable conjugate base corresponds to a higher acid ionization equilibrium constant and greater acidity.

Step 2: Evaluation
In ethanol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)), the negative charge in the ethoxide ion is localized on an oxygen atom and destabilized by the \(+I\) inductive effect of the ethyl group, making ethanol the weakest acid (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 16\)). In phenol (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}\)), the phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance delocalization of the negative charge into the benzene ring (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 10\)), making phenol stronger than ethanol. Carboxylic acids are much stronger acids than phenols because the carboxylate anion delocalizes negative charge equivalently between two highly electronegative oxygen atoms. Between acetic acid (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}\), \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 4.76\)) and chloroacetic acid (\(\mathrm{ClCH}_2\mathrm{COOH}\), \(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 2.86\)), the chlorine atom exerts a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect (\(-I\)), which disperses negative charge in the conjugate base and enhances acidity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct order of increasing acidic strength is Ethanol \(<\) Phenol \(<\) Acetic acid \(<\) Chloroacetic acid.

questiontext.text: Compound \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{O}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{Ph}\) can be prepared by the reaction of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The target compound \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{O}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{Ph}\) is phenyl benzoate, an aryl ester. Acylation of phenol with an acyl chloride in the presence of an organic base is a Schotten-Baumann type esterification.

Step 2: Evaluation
Phenol reacts with benzoyl chloride in the presence of pyridine to give phenyl benzoate. Pyridine acts as a base and catalyst by facilitating nucleophilic attack of the phenolic oxygen on the acyl carbon and removing the liberated hydrogen chloride, which shifts the equilibrium to completion:
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Pyridine}} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{O}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5 + \mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}^+\mathrm{Cl}^-\]Direct reaction between phenol and benzoic acid with sodium hydroxide fails because both species convert to anions, while benzaldehyde is not an acylating agent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Phenyl benzoate can be prepared by the reaction of phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of pyridine.

answer.text: Phenol and benzoic acid in the presence of NaOH
Phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of pyridine
Phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of \(\mathrm{ZnCl}_2\)
Phenol and benzaldehyde in the presence of palladium

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q05 - Reagent non-reactive with acetone and benzaldehyde

questiontext.text: The reagent which does not react with both, acetone and benzaldehyde.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fehling's solution is a mild alkaline copper(II) tartrate complex that selectively oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes. Ketones and aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's solution.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acetone is a ketone, lacking a formyl hydrogen atom, and therefore cannot be oxidized by mild oxidizing agents like Fehling's solution. Benzaldehyde is an aromatic aldehyde; electron donation from the aromatic \(\pi\)-system into the carbonyl carbon reduces its electrophilicity and hinders oxidation by Fehling's solution. Consequently, neither acetone nor benzaldehyde reacts with Fehling's solution. In contrast, both compounds react with nucleophilic reagents including sodium hydrogensulphite, phenyl hydrazine, and Grignard reagents.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Fehling's solution does not react with both acetone and benzaldehyde.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q06 - Identification of aldehyde failing Cannizzaro reaction

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cannizzaro's reaction is a disproportionation reaction exhibited by aldehydes that lack \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms when treated with concentrated alkali. Aldehydes containing \(\alpha\)-hydrogens undergo base-catalyzed aldol condensation instead.

Step 2: Evaluation
1-Methylcyclohexanecarbaldehyde has a quaternary \(\alpha\)-carbon bonded to three carbons and the formyl group, possessing no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom; hence it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO}\)) has an \(sp^2\) aromatic ring carbon directly attached to the formyl group with no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen, undergoing the Cannizzaro reaction. Formaldehyde (\(\mathrm{HCHO}\)) has no \(\alpha\)-carbon and no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen, undergoing the Cannizzaro reaction. Acetaldehyde (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}\)) possesses three \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms on its methyl group; upon treatment with concentrated base, it undergoes deprotonation and aldol condensation rather than Cannizzaro's reaction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Acetaldehyde, \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}\), does not give Cannizzaro's reaction.

questiontext.text: Which product is formed when the compound \(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}\) is treated with concentrated aqueous KOH solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO}\)) contains no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms. When heated with concentrated aqueous potassium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{KOH}\)), it undergoes Cannizzaro's disproportionation reaction, in which one molecule is oxidized to a carboxylic acid salt and another molecule is reduced to an alcohol.

Step 2: Evaluation
In concentrated aqueous potassium hydroxide, hydroxide ions attack the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde to form a tetrahedral intermediate. A hydride ion transfers to a second molecule of benzaldehyde, yielding benzoic acid and a benzyloxide ion. Rapid proton transfer in the presence of potassium counterions yields potassium benzoate (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOK}\)) and benzyl alcohol (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)):
\[2\,\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO} + \mathrm{KOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOK} + \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The mixture formed comprises potassium benzoate and benzyl alcohol, represented by the combined structure containing \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOK} + \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\).

Structure of 'A' and type of isomerism in the above reaction are respectively.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acid-catalyzed hydration of unsymmetrical alkynes in the presence of mercuric sulfate follows Markovnikov's rule. The hydroxyl group attaches to the more substituted carbon atom of the triple bond to yield an enol intermediate.

Step 2: Evaluation
Addition of water across propyne (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}\)) yields prop-1-en-2-ol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CH}_2\)) as intermediate 'A'. An enol is unstable with respect to its keto isomer; dynamic migration of a proton accompanied by relocation of the \(\pi\)-bond converts the enol into acetone (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)). This equilibrium between functional isomer forms differing by proton relocation is known as keto-enol tautomerism.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Intermediate 'A' is prop-1-en-2-ol, and the type of isomerism is tautomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q09 - Relationship between Grignard and hydroboration products

questiontext.text:
Compounds A and C in the following reaction are

\[\mathrm{CH_3CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) } \mathrm{CH_3MgBr}} (\mathrm{A}) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2SO_4}, \Delta} (\mathrm{B}) \xrightarrow{\text{Hydroboration oxidation}} (\mathrm{C})\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Addition of a methyl Grignard reagent to an aldehyde yields a secondary alcohol. Acid-catalyzed dehydration of that alcohol gives an alkene. Subsequent hydroboration-oxidation of the alkene produces an alcohol via anti-Markovnikov hydration.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acetaldehyde (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}\)) reacts with methylmagnesium bromide (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}\)) followed by aqueous workup to produce propan-2-ol as compound A:
\[\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3\quad(\mathrm{A})\]Dehydration of propan-2-ol with concentrated sulfuric acid and heat produces propene as compound B:
\[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4,\,\Delta} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2\quad(\mathrm{B})\]Hydroboration-oxidation of propene with diborane followed by basic hydrogen peroxide results in anti-Markovnikov addition of water, placing the hydroxyl group at the terminal position to give propan-1-ol as compound C:
\[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Hydroboration oxidation}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\quad(\mathrm{C})\]Propan-2-ol (A) and propan-1-ol (C) have identical molecular formula (\(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_8\mathrm{O}\)) and functional group, differing only in the position of the hydroxyl group on the carbon chain.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Compounds A and C are positional isomers.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q10 - Selective oxidation of methyl ketone with alkene

questiontext.text:
Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion?

\[\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-\overset{\overset{\displaystyle O}{\parallel}}{C}-CH_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-\overset{\overset{\displaystyle O}{\parallel}}{C}-OH}\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Converting a methyl ketone group (\(-\mathrm{COCH}_3\)) selectively into a carboxylic acid group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) without disturbing a non-conjugated carbon-carbon double bond requires the haloform reaction.

Step 2: Evaluation
Treatment with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{I}_2 + \mathrm{NaOH}\) forming hypoiodite, \(\mathrm{NaOI}\)) oxidizes methyl ketones to sodium carboxylates while precipitating yellow iodoform (\(\mathrm{CHI}_3\)). This reagent specifically attacks the methyl ketone functionality and leaves isolated or conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds intact. Subsequent acidification yields the unsaturated carboxylic acid. Tollens' reagent only oxidizes aldehydes, benzoyl peroxide is a radical initiator that initiates alkene polymerization, and tin in alkali is a reducing agent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The most suitable reagent for this conversion is \(\mathrm{I}_2\) and \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution.

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds will give butanone on oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oxidation of primary alcohols by strong oxidizing agents such as alkaline potassium permanganate (\(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\)) produces carboxylic acids, whereas oxidation of secondary alcohols produces ketones containing the same number of carbon atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation
Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)); oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) converts it into butanoic acid (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COOH}\)). Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}_3\)); oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) dehydrogenates the carbinol carbon without carbon-carbon bond cleavage, selectively yielding the four-carbon ketone butan-2-one (butanone, \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COCH}_3\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Butan-2-ol yields butanone upon oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) solution.

questiontext.text: In Clemmensen Reduction carbonyl compound is treated with

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Clemmensen reduction is a standard method for reducing aldehydes and ketones to their corresponding hydrocarbons by replacing the carbonyl oxygen atom with two hydrogen atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation
The reaction employs amalgamated zinc and concentrated hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{Zn/Hg} + \mathrm{HCl}\)):
\[>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O} + 4[\mathrm{H}] \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Zn(Hg)}/\mathrm{HCl}} >\mathrm{CH}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\]Nitric acid cannot be utilized because it is a strong oxidizing agent, whereas sodium amalgam in water or acid typically reduces carbonyl compounds to alcohols or pinacols.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In Clemmensen Reduction, the carbonyl compound is treated with zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid (Zinc amalgam + HCl).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALDEHYDES_KETONES_AND_CARBOXYLIC_ACIDS_MCQ_Q13 - Compounds that do not undergo aldol condensation

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds do not undergo aldol condensation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aldol condensation requires at least one acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom attached to the carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group, enabling base-promoted enolate generation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acetaldehyde (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}\)) contains three \(\alpha\)-hydrogens on its methyl group and readily undergoes aldol condensation. Acetone possesses six \(\alpha\)-hydrogens across two methyl groups and undergoes aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde has its formyl group bonded directly to an \(sp^2\) aromatic ring carbon with no hydrogen atom, having zero \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal has its formyl group bonded to a quaternary carbon bearing three methyl groups, also possessing zero \(\alpha\)-hydrogens. Consequently, neither benzaldehyde nor 2,2-dimethylpropanal can form an enolate to undergo aldol condensation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The compounds that do not undergo aldol condensation are benzaldehyde and 2,2-dimethylpropanal.

questiontext.text: Treatment of compound \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{O}-\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\underset{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{Ph}\) with NaOH solution yields

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Base-promoted hydrolysis of an ester by aqueous sodium hydroxide (saponification) cleaves the ester linkage to produce a carboxylate salt and an alcohol or phenol.

Step 2: Evaluation
Phenyl benzoate (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOC}_6\mathrm{H}_5\)) undergoes nucleophilic attack by hydroxide ion at the carbonyl carbon, producing sodium benzoate and phenol:
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOC}_6\mathrm{H}_5 + \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COONa} + \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}\]Because phenol is a weak acid (\(\mathrm{p}K_a \approx 10\)), it reacts immediately with sodium hydroxide in the basic solution to form sodium phenoxide and water:
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{ONa} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\]Therefore, in aqueous sodium hydroxide, the isolable reaction products are sodium phenoxide and sodium benzoate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Treatment of phenyl benzoate with aqueous sodium hydroxide yields sodium phenoxide and sodium benzoate.

questiontext.text: Which of the following conversions can be carried out by Clemmensen Reduction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Clemmensen reduction employs zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{Zn/Hg} + \mathrm{HCl}\)) to reduce the carbonyl group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)) of aldehydes and ketones into a methylene group (\(>\mathrm{CH}_2\)), producing alkanes.

Step 2: Evaluation
In cyclohexanone, reduction of the ring keto carbonyl group converts it into the cyclic alkane cyclohexane:
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Zn(Hg)}/\mathrm{HCl}} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\]In benzophenone (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COC}_6\mathrm{H}_5\)), reduction of the diaryl ketone carbonyl group converts it into diphenylmethane (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\)):
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COC}_6\mathrm{H}_5 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Zn(Hg)}/\mathrm{HCl}} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\]Converting benzaldehyde into benzyl alcohol is a reduction to an alcohol rather than a hydrocarbon, and converting benzoyl chloride into benzaldehyde is Rosenmund reduction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The conversions achievable by Clemmensen reduction are cyclohexanone into cyclohexane, and benzophenone into diphenyl methane.

questiontext.text: Through which of the following reactions number of carbon atoms can be increased in the chain?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Increasing the number of carbon atoms in a chain requires a synthetic reaction that forms a new carbon-carbon covalent bond between reactants.

Step 2: Evaluation
In a Grignard reaction, an organomagnesium reagent acts as a carbanion equivalent that attacks an electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a new carbon-carbon bond and extending the carbon chain length. In aldol condensation, an enolate carbanion nucleophile attacks another carbonyl compound to form a carbon-carbon bond, yielding a product with a longer carbon chain. In contrast, the Cannizzaro reaction is a redox disproportionation of aldehydes involving hydride shift without carbon-carbon coupling. The Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction halogenates carboxylic acids at the \(\alpha\)-position without altering the number of carbon atoms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The reactions that increase the number of carbon atoms in the chain are the Grignard reaction and aldol condensation.

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Benzophenone (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COC}_6\mathrm{H}_5\)) is a diaryl ketone. Ketones can be prepared by Friedel-Crafts acylation of aromatic rings or by reaction of acid chlorides with dialkyl/diarylcadmium reagents.

Step 2: Evaluation
Reaction of benzoyl chloride with benzene in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\)) is a Friedel-Crafts acylation that forms benzophenone:
\[\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCl} + \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{AlCl}_3} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COC}_6\mathrm{H}_5 + \mathrm{HCl}\]Reaction of benzoyl chloride with diphenylcadmium produces benzophenone because organocadmium reagents are less nucleophilic than Grignard reagents and do not add further to the ketone:
\[2\,\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCl} + (\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_2\mathrm{Cd} \longrightarrow 2\,\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COC}_6\mathrm{H}_5 + \mathrm{CdCl}_2\]Reaction of benzoyl chloride with phenylmagnesium chloride proceeds further to give triphenylmethanol tertiary alcohol. Reaction of benzene with carbon monoxide and \(\mathrm{HCl}\) in the presence of \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3/\mathrm{CuCl}\) is the Gattermann-Koch reaction, yielding benzaldehyde rather than benzophenone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Benzophenone can be obtained by reacting benzoyl chloride + Benzene + \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\), and by reacting benzoyl chloride + Diphenyl cadmium.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the correct representation for intermediate of nucleophilic addition reaction to the given carbonyl compound (A)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a carbonyl compound, the carbonyl carbon is \(sp^2\)-hybridized and adopts a trigonal planar geometry. Nucleophilic addition involves attack of the nucleophile (\(\mathrm{Nu}\)) perpendicular to this plane, rehybridizing the carbon from \(sp^2\) to \(sp^3\) and generating a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because the planar substrate presents two enantiotopic faces with equal accessibility, nucleophilic attack can occur from either the front face or the rear face of the molecular plane. Attack from one face yields a tetrahedral intermediate in which substituent \(b\) projects forward (wedge) and substituent \(a\) projects backward (dash), with the alkoxide oxygen and nucleophile accommodated in a tetrahedral configuration. Attack from the opposite face produces the enantiomeric tetrahedral intermediate with inverted wedge/dash orientations for substituents \(a\) and \(b\). Representations depicting cross or planar geometries fail to convey the true three-dimensional \(sp^3\) tetrahedral geometry of the intermediate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both enantiomeric three-dimensional representations depicting a tetrahedral geometry with properly directed wedged and dashed bonds for substituents \(a\) and \(b\) correctly represent the reaction intermediate.
